panels.description:
The number of concurrent connections processed by vmauth reached one of limits. Possible solutions:
- increase global limit with flag -maxConcurrentRequests
- increase limit with flag: -maxConcurrentPerUserRequests for all users or with config option `max_concurrent_requests` per user.
- deploy additional vmauth replicas
- check requests latency at backend service and allocate resources to it if needed
panels.title: Concurrent limit reached

Shows the percentage of open file descriptors compared to the limit set in the OS.
Reaching the limit of open files can cause various issues and must be prevented.

See how to change limits here https://medium.com/@muhammadtriwibowo/set-permanently-ulimit-n-open-files-in-ubuntu-4d61064429a

panels.description: Shows number of generated error and warning messages in logs. Non-zero value may be a sign of connectivity or misconfiguration errors.
panels.title: Logging rate

panels.description:
Shows the backend request error rate per user.
The value can be higher than the request error rate if:
1. A single request is retried multiple times due to transient network errors, such as proxy idle timeout misconfiguration or sockets being closed by the OS.
2. The request fails and is retried on other backends because of configured retry_status_codes.
panels.title: Requests backend error rate

panels.description:
This metric helps identify slow-uploading clients. Elevated buffering percentiles together with a drop in incoming request rate, in the absence of CPU, memory, or upstream saturation, usually indicate slow client uploads (for example, a client on EDGE connection).

Slow clients can hold concurrency slots for extended periods, causing vmauth to hit concurrency limits and reject requests even when upstream services have sufficient capacity. Increasing `-requestBufferSize` decouples client upload speed from request processing, reducing concurrency pressure and protecting vmauth and upstream services, at the cost of higher memory usage.

This metric is available only when `-requestBufferSize` is non-zero (default: 32KiB). The maximum time vmauth waits for the request body to be fully read (or for the buffer to be filled) is controlled by `-maxQueueDuration` (default: 10s).

Read more in [request body buffering](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#request-body-buffering) documentation.
panels.title: Request body buffering duration P99
